speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To help me determine the cause, how long has this been going on, and have you noticed any redness, warmth, or morning stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of a sudden catch-and-pull mechanism while playing football is highly suggestive of an acute injury. Can you describe the exact nature of the movement at the time of injury, and is there a specific point on the finger that is most tender to touch?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Rupture)

The inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, combined with the finger resting in an extended position and a history of a direct pulling force, is classic for a mallet finger. I am confident this is the correct diagnosis based on your specific physical exam findings.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
